title: Book One · Chapter 169: The Man Who Comes Home
story:
Dad is quiet at supper. He eats slowly and looks at the invitation after he has finished. Ronan waits until Mum has sat down with her tea.

“Is something wrong?” he asks.

Dad turns the paper between his fingers. “Not with your room.”

Ronan puts his own hands flat on the table. He wants to hear Dad's next words. He waits. He asks no more questions.

Dad says he did not like reading the old shop card. Even after Ronan put it away, Dad kept thinking about it. He did close the shop. There were mistakes. He once promised too much. He told Ronan a little about that. He will explain more when Ronan is older.

“But I do not want visitors to read only about my old mistakes,” Dad says.

“You mean your old shop?”

Dad nods.

Ronan looks at the invitation, with the blue box and the foolish tree. “I want you there, Dad. You come home to us every day.”

Mum's hand stops near her cup. Dad looks at him.

“Then those are the words for my card,” Ronan says. “Not the other story.”

Dad breathes out. He puts the invitation flat on the table. He smooths the fold with his hand.

“You changed the card and the picture list. I know that.”

“You can just come and look. You can stay quiet about the stool.”

“I might want to say something about the stool. It is a good stool.”

Mum laughs softly. “It has become a very well-known stool.”

They all look at it by the doorway. There is a clean folded cloth on its seat. They have talked so much about this little seat. Mum smiles and touches the clean cloth.

Dad cannot change the Saturday work answer. There are still jobs to finish. “Shall I describe the room again?” Ronan asks. Then Dad can find it quickly if he comes.

Dad says yes. Ronan tells him to start at the school gate. Then he must cross the hall to the small room. Dad can stay quiet and look at things there. He can just come and look. Mum listens and corrects the turn by the hall.

After supper Dad washes the bowls. Ronan dries them. Their hands meet once over the largest bowl. Dad holds it until Ronan has a good grip, then lets go.

“I was not trying to make you feel small,” Ronan says.

“I know. You wanted to help. But your card still made me feel small.”

Ronan nods. Dad speaks quietly. Ronan looks down at the bowl. He loves Dad and wanted to help. But the card still upset Dad. Ronan put it away and did not show anyone. He is glad about that now.

They finish the bowls. Dad puts the blue box away. The invitation goes back in his shirt pocket. Mum opens her borrowed pattern book. She will return it soon. Tonight she reads a little more.

Ronan sits near the window. He can see the gate and the little grey table under its cover. He is still disappointed about the work hours. He is also glad Dad asked for the way to the room.

He wishes Dad could come on time. He is still glad Dad asked for the way. He can feel both things at once. Dad says good night. Ronan closes his book and says good night too. He asks no more questions about Saturday.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：grip＝握牢；describe＝描述；upset＝使人难过。

情节提示：grip＝抓牢；pattern book＝缝制图样书；invitation＝邀请卡。

理解：1. Dad 担心参观者只看见自己的哪一部分？2. Ronan 怎样重新表达对父亲的邀请？
